workingTitle: Tiny solar explosions reveal reconnection near the Sun's visible surface
publicationStatus: Peer-reviewed Astrophysical Journal Letters article first made public on arXiv 16 October 2026; NSO release published 20 November 2026
coreFacts: The study identified 14 unique Ellerman bombs in four 6.3-minute raster scans of an emerging-flux region observed by DKIST on 18 June 2024.
The Visible Spectro-Polarimeter recorded hydrogen-beta, sodium D1, and iron 6302 angstrom lines simultaneously.
Multiline inversions inferred localized heating of roughly 150 to 800 kelvin, with a mean near 300 kelvin.
Most events lay near mixed-polarity magnetic fields and showed weak upward and downward plasma flows consistent with magnetic reconnection in the photosphere.
Bifrost simulations reproduced several spectral features but generally produced stronger heating and faster flows than observed.

sources.label: Multiline Spectropolarimetric Evidence for Photospheric Reconnection in Ellerman Bombs from DKIST

sourceStatus: Peer-reviewed ApJL paper verified through its full arXiv text; the National Solar Observatory release corroborates the interpretation and publication context.
caveats: The sample contains 14 events from one emerging-flux region and is not a survey of the whole Sun.
The roughly six-minute raster cadence cannot resolve the full time evolution or total energy budget of individual events.
The simulations were a qualitative comparison and were not designed to reproduce the exact observed conditions.
